scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After an overnight maintenance window, pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports
pings to pc2 (200.1.1.2) are 100% lost, and pc2 reports the same
toward pc1. Yet monitoring shows the router1<->router2 eBGP
session Established with prefixes exchanged, and pc1 can still
ping BOTH of router2's addresses (193.10.11.2 and 200.1.1.1).
Identify what is dropping the traffic.

injection.action: add an iptables FORWARD rule dropping all transit ICMP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router2 iptables FORWARD chain
Mechanism: a DROP rule for protocol icmp sits in router2's FORWARD
  chain, so any ICMP packet router2 must FORWARD (pc1<->pc2 transit
  in either direction) is discarded at the firewall layer. Traffic
  addressed TO router2 itself traverses INPUT, not FORWARD, which
  is why pc1 can still ping 193.10.11.2 and 200.1.1.1. The BGP
  session is TCP, not ICMP, so it stays Established and all
  prefixes remain exchanged -- routing is completely healthy; the
  drop is purely at the packet-filter layer.
Localization: router2
Root cause: extraneous iptables FORWARD DROP rule for ICMP on
  router2
Fix: `iptables -D FORWARD -p icmp -j DROP` on router2
scenario.fix_spec:
Remove the DROP rule on router2 -- `iptables -D FORWARD -p icmp -j DROP`.
Transit pings between pc1 and pc2 succeed again immediately; no routing or
BGP change is needed.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: router2’s host firewall (iptables/nftables) in the IPv4 FORWARD chain.

Mechanism: ICMP echo traffic between pc1 (195.11.14.2) and pc2 (200.1.1.2) must be forwarded across router2 (between eth0 193.10.11.2 and eth1 200.1.1.1). On router2, the FORWARD chain contains an explicit “-p icmp -j DROP,” so transit ICMP packets are discarded. Pings to router2’s own interfaces (193.10.11.2 and 200.1.1.1) succeed because they are processed by the INPUT chain, not FORWARD, which matches the symptom.

Localization: router2, packet filter. Evidence:
- iptables -S on router2 shows: “-A FORWARD -p icmp -j DROP.”
- nft list ruleset on router2 shows table ip filter/chain FORWARD with “meta l4proto icmp … drop,” and counters incrementing (counter packets 6 bytes 504), confirming live drops.
- Routing is otherwise correct: router2 kernel table has 195.11.14.0/24 via 193.10.11.1 (BGP) and 200.1.1.0/24 directly on eth1, and router1/pc hosts have proper defaults. pc1 can ping router2’s addresses, proving L3 reachability and eBGP adjacency health.

Root cause: A firewall rule added during the maintenance window is dropping ICMP in the FORWARD path on router2.

Corrective fix: Remove or adjust the rule to permit ICMP forwarding. For example, on router2: iptables -D FORWARD -p icmp -j DROP (or delete the equivalent nftables rule), and optionally add explicit allows for icmp type echo-request/echo-reply. Ensure persistence by updating the firewall configuration files or service to retain the corrected policy.
